content: 1. Ivabradine's levels or effects can be increased by drugs that inhibit the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors or consider alternative therapies. 2. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates or replace with alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. 3. Tetracycline increases lemborexant levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 4. Tetracycline increases lurbinectedin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Magnesium chloride reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Magnesium citrate reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Magnesium hydroxide reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Magnesium oxide reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Magnesium sulfate reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Tetracycline and methoxyflurane coadministration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Tetracycline and methyl aminolevulinate coadministration increases the risk of photosensitization due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Tetracycline reduces the effects of oral microbiota therapies by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota therapy. 13. Tetracycline increases midazolam intranasal levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, as this may prolong sedation. 14. Tetracycline reduces the effects of nafcillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Tetracycline increases naloxegol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Tetracycline increases neratinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 17. Tetracycline increases nirogacestat levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Tetracycline increases olaparib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 19. Tetracycline increases omaveloxolone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor for adverse effects. Further reduce to 50 mg/day if necessary. 20. Tetracycline reduces oxacillin effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Tetracycline increases pacritinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Tetracycline and palovarotene coadministration may increase the risk of benign intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri). Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Tetracycline increases pancuronium effects by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 24. Tetracycline increases pemigatinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. 25. Tetracycline reduces the effects of penicillin G aqueous by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Tetracycline reduces the effects of penicillin VK by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 27. Tetracycline increases pexidartinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. 28. Phenobarbital decreases tetracycline levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 29. Phenytoin decreases tetracycline levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Polysaccharide iron reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Primidone decreases tetracycline levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Tetracycline increases rapacuronium effects by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Tetracycline increases repotrectinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3–5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 34. Tetracycline increases rocuronium effects by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Rose hips reduce tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Tetracycline increases selumetinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose as per the drug monograph. 37. Tetracycline increases siponimod levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 38. Sodium bicarbonate reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. 39. Sodium citrate/citric acid reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. 40. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 41. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer tetracyclines at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 42. Strontium ranelate reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Suspend strontium ranelate during antibiotic therapy. 43. Tetracycline increases succinylcholine effects by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Tetracycline increases tazemetostat levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per the drug monograph. 45. Tetracycline reduces temocillin effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 46. Tetracycline and tretinoin coadministration increases the risk of phototoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 47. Tetracycline and topical tretinoin coadministration increases the risk of phototoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 48. Tripotassium dicitrato bismuthate reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 49. Tucatinib increases tetracycline levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 50. Tetracycline reduces the effects of the live typhoid vaccine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 51. Tetracycline increases vecuronium effects by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 52. Tetracycline increases venetoclax levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for toxicities. 53. Tetracycline increases acalabrutinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. 54. Tetracycline increases atogepant levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Tetracycline increases avanafil levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the maximum dose of avanafil to 50 mg, not exceeding once every 24 hours, when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 56. Tetracycline reduces the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Bosentan decreases tetracycline levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Tetracycline increases brexpiprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor. 59. Tetracycline increases buprenorphine subdermal implant levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for signs of overmedication. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary. 60. Tetracycline increases buprenorphine long-acting injection levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor plasma levels to ensure adequacy. Transition to a formulation that allows dose adjustments if toxicity occurs. 61. Tetracycline increases cabazitaxel levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Tetracycline increases cabozantinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Tetracycline increases cannabidiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 64. Tetracycline increases capivasertib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the capivasertib dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 65. Tetracycline reduces cefdinir effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Tetracycline reduces cefditoren effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Tetracycline reduces cefoxitin effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely.
